sourceNote: Hand-authored, not ETS material. The Item with the published sample's shape is build-a-sentence-reference-item.json. These three Items are the frame shapes the gate has to accept: a frame that begins with a blank, a frame that is nothing but blanks and the sentence-final punctuation (a full reorder), and the conventional fixed-opening frame. Every tile is lowercase, including the one that starts the sentence, so the starting tile is not given away (docs/adr/0009). Read by buildASentenceConformance.test.ts, sentenceScorer.test.ts and sentenceFrame.test.ts; the client mirrors the same three shapes inline in client/test/BuildSentenceTask.test.tsx (the client suite reads no files).

items.prompt: What did you ask the department for?
items.note: The sentence's first word is a TILE, and it is lowercase: 'we'. Six blanks, seven tiles, 'asking' the distractor (it forces the past tense against the fixed tail). Under the old rules this Item was illegal twice over — the frame did not fix the opening word, and the opening word would have had to carry a capital.

items.prompt: How much longer do you have?
items.note: The ramp's end state: only the final period is fixed. Nine blanks, ten tiles — the new ceiling — with 'extending' the distractor.

The conventional shape, unchanged: the frame fixes the opening word and the sentence-final punctuation. Four blanks, five tiles, 'arrived' the distractor. It is here as the control — widening the gate must not stop accepting what it already accepted.
